fields.name: clientId
fields.label: Client ID
fields.hint: The remote signs in through a Spotify app of your own. On developer.spotify.com: Dashboard, Create app (any name; tick Web API; add the Redirect URI below), then copy the Client ID from its Settings. Spotify wants the app's owner to have Premium, and lets an app in development mode serve up to five accounts: add them under User Management.

fields.name: clientSecret
fields.label: Client secret
fields.hint: Under the Client ID: View client secret. It stays in this scene's settings on the frame, like a password.

fields.name: signIn
fields.label: Sign-in address
fields.hint: Once the frame shows Sign in: open the sign-in page it links to (its QR code on the frame, or a new tab from the editor's preview), press Agree, then copy the address the browser lands on and paste it here. That page does not open, which is expected: its address has the code in it. The frame signs in with it and empties this field; paste a new one to sign in again, as another account say.

fields.name: redirectUri
fields.label: Redirect URI
fields.hint: The Redirect URI you added to your Spotify app, letter for letter. Spotify allows http only for 127.0.0.1, so keep this one unless you have an https page of your own.

fields.name: speaker
fields.label: Speaker to start on
fields.hint: Where Play starts the music when nothing plays anywhere: a Spotify Connect speaker by its name, as the Spotify app lists it under Devices. A frame with a speaker can be one when it runs a Spotify Connect receiver (Raspotify on a Raspberry Pi, say). Empty: where music played last.

options.label: Auto: high contrast where the panel shows no color

spotifyRemote.name: Spotify remote
spotifyRemote.description: What plays on your Spotify account, and a remote for it: play and pause, skip, seek, shuffle, repeat, the volume and the heart, the speaker it plays on, and a playlist to start. Signs in with a Spotify app of your own (Premium).
